title: Observed flow seasonality and calibration-period context: 29 gauges, 2020–2025
sections: The retained record contains 59,701 original daily records for 29 gauges in 2020–2025, including 59,700 numeric daily means and one original nonnumeric Rat/P record. Of 174 gauge-years, 149 have every calendar day numeric and 144 also have an approved flag on every day. There are 1936 complete months and 629 complete seasons.

Calendar-period comparisons preserve 148 complete months and 33 complete seasons within years that lack a complete annual record. A complete season is usable for its own mean and volume comparison. Annual-volume fractions require the complete annual denominator. All missing numeric dates, nonnumeric originals and source flags remain available in the companion tables.

sections: Seasonal flow contrasts in the 2023 observation period

At Eighteenmile Creek below Pendleton, the 2023 summer mean was 58.663 cfs, 33.85% above the median of its other complete summers. Autumn averaged 27.963 cfs, 46.56% below the corresponding autumn median. Summer carried 21.61% of complete 2023 volume compared with a 14.83% median share; autumn carried 10.19% compared with 18.31%. These temporal contrasts identify different hydrologic sampling contexts within the same annual period.

sections.caption: Winter combines January, February and December of the stated calendar year. Ratios use complete seasons independently of annual completeness.

sections: Each selected year is compared with other complete periods at the same gauge. The complete_numeric basis admits numeric values with their retained original flags. The fully_approved_complete basis requires A on every target and reference-period day; A:e remains both approved and estimated. Period-level reference years and annual-fraction reference years are recorded separately. For Eighteenmile 2023, approved summer and autumn comparisons include 2025, while approved annual-fraction references exclude 2025 because its winter contains provisional values.

sections: Annual flow allocation and observed flow-duration context

Daily flow-duration values use the R-7 observed quantile at 1 minus exceedance probability: Q5 is the high-flow P95 and Q95 is the low-flow P05. The table below reports the median across each gauge's complete years of the share of annual volume carried by days at or above that year's P95. The inclusive threshold retains ties. At Stevens Creek (02196000), this median share is 60.59% across six complete years; at Kettle Creek (02193340), 50.45% across six. Eighteenmile's six-year median is 25.05%. Augusta Canal's 6.77% uses only 2020 and 2025. These are observed within-gauge distributions with different record support.

sections: The record is six dated years, with fewer complete years at some gauges. Reference minima, medians and maxima describe those actual years and are not confidence intervals or long-term climatological normals. Gauge volumes retain their individual contributing areas and are not summed across nested stations. Streamflow context does not supply constituent concentrations or annual nitrogen, phosphorus or sediment export. Catchment boundaries, outlet/network position, source-period coverage and any documented transfers or regulation still need to match the intended scientific comparison.
Reproducible periods, units and original source records

Daily decimal discharge values are added with exact scaled integers before conversion using 0.028316846592 m³ per cubic foot and 86,400 nominal seconds per day. Unknown days contribute no invented flow. Complete-period volume is absent when any selected calendar day lacks a numeric value; observed-period volume remains the sum of retained known days.

Mean ratios compare daily mean discharge, while volume ratios retain actual period duration. Leap-year February and the calendar-year winter can have an extra day. Annual fractions remain on a complete calendar-year denominator. Fully approved references are separate explicit selections, and estimated or revised flags remain visible within them.

The frozen input is the exact flow-data JSON extracted from the retained 29-gauge source edition. All 77 original response/inventory files retain exact SHA-256 identities; 56 supplied the daily flow records. Original source ID, JSON value-series/record position or RDB line number accompanies every retained high/low-flow date. The Horse Creek 2024-09-24 Rat/P source row remains nonnumeric.
